catalog.name: Omega Centauri
catalog.description: Omega Centauri is a globular star cluster in the Milky Way, about 5,426 parsecs away. That published distance locates the cluster, not its individual stars.

facts.label: Distance from the Sun
facts.note: Combined Gaia EDR3, HST and literature distance, Table 2, NGC 5139. One cluster scale; individual stellar distances are not recovered.

source.label: Baumgardt & Vasiliev (2021), Accurate distances to Galactic globular clusters through a combination of Gaia EDR3, HST and literature data, Table 2, NGC 5139: combined distance 5.426 +/- 0.047 kpc. Full downloaded paper bytes.
ESO/INAF-VST/OmegaCAM eso1119b native TIFF and embedded AVM. The common observation-frame center is an adopted registration origin, not a new dynamical centroid measurement.

facts.label: Classification
facts.note: Observed integrated cluster starlight; the selected oblate Gaussian profile supplies conditional depth for finite display-emission components.

source.label: D’Souza & Rix (2013), Mass estimates from stellar proper motions: the mass of omega Centauri, Table 1 and section 4.3. Eight projected Gaussian components define a conditional oblate light prior, not resolved stellar depths.
